provenance.notes: B2b family batch, rfq archetype. Licensed, compliance-driven trade: copy never promises a passed inspection, never interprets the fire code and never names a code section or licence number. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Look up when the tag says the next annual inspection is due, sign up for reminders, and a plain note on the periodic maintenance and hydrostatic testing the client performs
pageStructurePlus.why: Most small businesses only think about extinguishers when the tag runs out or an inspector visits. A reminder signup turns that moment into a standing account.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Upload the deficiency notice from the fire marshal or insurer, see which items the client can correct, the visit window, and the paperwork returned after service
pageStructurePlus.why: A deficiency notice comes with a deadline. Owners holding one choose the fire protection company that says how fast it can clear the list.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Restaurant hood suppression inspections, fusible link changes, nozzle checks, K-class extinguishers, and coordination with the hood cleaning company
pageStructurePlus.why: Restaurant owners buy hood suppression and extinguisher service together. A dedicated page wins the account that pays for both.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Which fire extinguisher class suits offices, shops, kitchens, server rooms and vehicles, mounting and signage, cabinets, and new-unit sales
pageStructurePlus.why: New tenants and new businesses don't know what to buy. A plain guide brings them to the service company before the big-box store.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Monthly and annual emergency light and exit sign tests, battery and lamp replacement, and written logs left for the inspector
pageStructurePlus.why: Exit lights fail the same inspection as extinguishers. Bundling them gives the fire safety visit more value per stop.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Hands-on extinguisher training sessions for employees, what a session covers, group sizes, and the attendance record the client provides
pageStructurePlus.why: Insurers and safety managers ask for employee training. Offering it on the page opens a second budget at the same customer.

openers.line: Your Google listing for extinguisher service has no website, so a new restaurant owner told to get their fire extinguishers tagged has no way to check you before calling.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What that restaurant owner could open instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing links to a Facebook page with fire safety tips and truck photos. A facilities manager needs to see inspection services, coverage and how to book, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap the Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the most recent post date.
openers.linkLine: A fire protection site built for the facilities buyer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page that lists extinguisher service and nothing else. Buyers comparing fire protection vendors want inspections, hood systems and exit lights in one place.
openers.hook: Open the site and note what's missing or stale: services, a form, an old year.
openers.linkLine: Same fire safety company, complete and current: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your fire safety site's service list runs off the screen. Store managers usually look up an extinguisher company right after an inspector leaves.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same extinguisher service site on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to book an annual extinguisher inspection except calling. A request form with the address, unit count and tag date would fill your route without phone tag.
openers.hook: Check their site and listing for a booking or request form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: An inspection request that asks for unit count and tag date: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts of restaurant hood suppression service show work most extinguisher companies can't do, and a restaurant owner searching for it will never scroll that far.
openers.hook: Find one hood system or kitchen post. If there's none, use another specialty service they show.
openers.linkLine: Your hood suppression service on its own page: {demo-link}

openers.line: A review from a shop owner saying your tech cleared their fire marshal list the same week is what the next owner with a deficiency notice needs to read.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about speed or an inspection. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews next to the deficiency request: {demo-link}

openers.line: When business insurance renews, underwriters ask for current extinguisher tags and inspection records. Owners search for fire safety service that week.
openers.hook: Use any time; sharper in the months when local commercial policies commonly renew. Name the month if you know it.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the insurance renewal rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: When a cook discharges an extinguisher on a grease fire at nine at night, the owner needs it recharged before the next service. If your fire safety line rings out, they call the next one.
openers.hook: Call their number in the evening and note whether it rings out or offers an after-hours option.
openers.linkLine: A fire safety page that takes the recharge call after hours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring an extinguisher technician. Good techs check whether a fire protection company looks established before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or listing. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A fire protection site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your service trucks cover towns well beyond {City}, but nothing online lists them. A business two towns over assumes the nearest fire extinguisher company is someone else.
openers.hook: Look for service mentions or reviews from nearby towns. Name the furthest one.
openers.linkLine: Coverage pages for your extinguisher routes: {demo-link}

openers.line: Chains and property managers want one annual fire safety contract for every location, billed together. A page that offers it gets you past the single-store price comparison.
openers.hook: Only if they serve multi-location customers. Look for chains or managers in reviews.

openers.line: Facilities buyers ask a fire protection vendor for their state licence and insurance before the first inspection. A page that shows the ones you hold answers it early.
openers.hook: Look for licence or insurance mentions on their listing or truck. Never claim a licence or number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licensing and insurance on one fire safety page: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like your extinguisher route grew store by store from owners who know you. When a store sells, the new owner searches for fire safety service instead of reading the old tag.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or posts about long-time customers. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Where a new store owner would find you: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is real fire protection work. A job like that belongs on a page a facilities manager can forward before they request an inspection.
openers.hook: Pick their newest service post and name it: the building type and the fire safety work done.
openers.linkLine: That job on a fire safety project page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is solid fire protection work.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and couldn't find anywhere a business owner could book an extinguisher inspection or send a fire marshal's deficiency list. I put together a sample fire safety page with an inspection request and a deficiency upload, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried between service calls. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has an inspection request with unit count and tag date, a page for clearing fire marshal deficiencies, and separate pages for hood suppression and exit lights. If it's not useful, say so and I'll leave you alone.

IF NO:

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a fire safety company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which a handful of new annual accounts covers."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, at the end of a route day?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: The fire marshal sends people to us.
objections.handler: "Good. Those owners still look you up before calling, and the site lets them upload the deficiency list so you show up with the right parts."

objections.objection: Our customers renew every year. We don't need new ones.
objections.handler: "Renewals are the best part of this trade. The site is for the store that sells, the new tenant and the chain that wants one fire safety vendor for every location."

objections.objection: We're a small route, not a big fire protection company.
objections.handler: "That's who this is for. A small extinguisher route with a clean site and a reminder signup looks as steady as a big outfit to a store owner."

objections.objection: I can't say what the code requires on a website. It's a liability.
objections.handler: "Agreed, and the site doesn't. It describes the services you perform and says to confirm requirements with the local fire marshal. You approve every word."

objections.objection: Big national fire companies win the chains.
objections.handler: "Some do. Regional chains and property managers often want a local vendor who answers the phone. A multi-site page shows you can handle every location."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's an inspection request, a deficiency upload and tag-date reminders. A few new annual accounts pay for it."

Want me to leave it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — a lot of businesses around {City} renew insurance and get asked for current extinguisher tags this time of year. Thought of you.

The fire safety site is still here whenever you want it, same price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a handful of new annual inspection accounts, not to one extinguisher sale.
The inspection request and the reminder signup are the core. Price everything else as additions.
Price specialty pages one at a time: hood suppression, exit lights, sprinkler inspection and training each sell to a different budget.
Have the owner approve every sentence about inspections and never let the page interpret the code.
Charge for the multi-site account page separately; it wins chains and property managers.
Keep monthly add-ons below one small store's annual inspection so they never feel heavy.

lineItems.description: Max with address, unit count by type, tag date, hood system checkbox and a route-day picker.
Max with notice upload, deadline field, item checklist and a text alert to the owner.
Max with reminders by email and text before the due month and a one-click booking link.
Max when the page covers a full service, such as hood suppression or exit lights, with its own request form.
Max with a location list upload, one schedule for all sites and a combined invoice explanation.
Max when each page names the business districts and route days served in that town.

withoutAI.whoPays: The hood cleaner, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The hood cleaner who works the same restaurants as your suppression techs needs a site that books by kitchen size."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Hood cleaning and suppression service share every restaurant and trade referrals weekly.

withoutAI.whoPays: The fire alarm or sprinkler contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "If you sub sprinkler or alarm work to another company, they need the same inspection request page you have."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same buyer, same fire marshal, separate licences, so they refer rather than compete.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The restaurant group whose hoods you inspect has a menu site that's slow on a phone. Your introduction gets me a meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Restaurant owners trust the fire safety tech who keeps them open.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The commercial insurance agents who send you clients needing current extinguisher tags have websites from years ago. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents and fire safety vendors share commercial clients and refer constantly.

withoutAI.route: Safety equipment and first aid suppliers
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The first aid cabinet company on your routes visits the same businesses monthly. Their reorder page needs work."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Route-based suppliers share stops and recommend each other.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The manager whose buildings get your fire extinguisher tags every year has a tenant portal nobody uses. You can get me in the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the vendor who keeps their buildings inspection-ready.

withAI.route: Booking assistant for the hood cleaner
withAI.pitchLine: "Restaurants describe their hood and cooking volume, and the assistant books the hood cleaning on a closed night and lines it up with suppression service."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built once around the fire safety client's restaurants, sold through their trust.

withAI.route: Inspection report summariser for insurance agents
withAI.pitchLine: "Agents drop in a client's fire safety inspection reports, and the assistant drafts a plain summary of open items for the renewal file."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents chase this paperwork every renewal. It also routes open items back to the fire safety client.

withAI.pitchLine: "Managers upload a fire marshal's report, and the assistant sorts each item by vendor: extinguishers, alarms, sprinklers or exit lights."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers juggle several fire vendors. Sorting the list saves them hours.

withAI.route: Reorder assistant for the safety supplier
withAI.pitchLine: "Businesses tell the assistant what was used from the first aid cabinet, and it drafts the restock order before the next route stop."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps businesses on the supplier's route.

withAI.route: Pre-inspection checklist assistant for the restaurant group
withAI.pitchLine: "Each location manager gets a weekly walk-through checklist drafted from that kitchen's last fire and health inspection reports, so nothing repeats."
withAI.whyItWorks: Groups with several kitchens fear repeat findings; the fire safety client already sees every report.

withAI.route: Inspection scheduling assistant for the sprinkler partner
withAI.pitchLine: "Building owners pick an inspection window, and the assistant books the sprinkler partner and the extinguisher visit on the same day."
withAI.whyItWorks: One visit for the owner, two vendors served.

softwareAI.name: Tag-date reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A month before each account's annual extinguisher inspection, the owner gets a text with two route days to pick from."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their customer list with last inspection month and phone numbers.

softwareAI.name: Route-day booking calendar
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers book their fire safety inspection only on the days your truck is already in their area, so the route stays tight."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their route days by area and the time each stop usually takes.

softwareAI.name: Digital inspection report with photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Techs log each extinguisher by location with a photo and condition, and the owner gets a clean inspection report before the truck leaves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their current inspection form and a tech willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Deficiency notice reader
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners upload the fire marshal's notice, and it pulls out each extinguisher, exit light and hood item into a draft work order for the office to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a set of past notices with the work orders they produced. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for recharges
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A restaurant calls after a discharge, gets a text asking how many extinguishers and what type, and the tech calls back ready to load the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal for inspection records
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners and safety managers download every fire safety inspection report and invoice, any time an insurer or inspector asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the digital report. Needs customer logins and report history.

softwareAI.name: Office call answering on route days
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers the fire protection line while everyone's on the route, takes the address and unit count, and books the inspection slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the booking calendar and the questions they ask on every call. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Unit inventory by location
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every extinguisher at every account, with type, size, location in the building and the year of the next major service."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, built from the digital reports. Needs one full route cycle of data.

softwareAI.name: Maintenance and hydro test due list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month, the office gets the list of extinguishers coming due for internal maintenance or hydro testing, grouped by route."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the unit inventory. Needs the client's service intervals as they apply them.

softwareAI.name: Quote writer for new-site placements
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The tech walks a new tenant space and talks through it, and a quote for extinguishers, cabinets, signage and mounting is drafted for approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their price list and past placement quotes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Multi-site account dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A chain's safety manager sees every location's fire safety status on one screen: inspected, due, or open deficiencies."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, once a multi-location account signs. Needs the portal and the account's location list.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot for inspection and service questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you service hood systems' and 'what do I need for a new shop' from the company's own approved answers, then books the extinguisher inspection."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs approved answers only, with no code interpretation. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Truck stock and parts tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Know what each service truck carries: spare extinguishers, tags, seals, gauges and fusible links, and what to restock before tomorrow's route."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the parts list and a tech to log usage.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for fire safety customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a shop owner thanks the tech for an extinguisher visit online, a short thank-you naming that inspection is ready for the owner to post."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Annual invoicing by route
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Fire extinguisher inspection invoices go out the day each route is finished, with parts and recharges added from the tech's report."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their accounting system and the digital report.

softwareAI.name: Training session booking and attendance
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Employers book hands-on extinguisher training, staff sign in on a phone, and the attendance record lands in the customer portal."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their training format and session sizes.

softwareAI.name: Inspection notes translator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deficiency notes and fire safety instructions for kitchen staff, translated into the languages each restaurant's crew speaks, reviewed by the owner."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the owner's review of each translation. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Bid notice watcher for fire protection
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Public agencies post extinguisher and exit light service contracts. The watcher flags the ones near your routes with due dates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the portals they're registered on. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tech applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for extinguisher technician roles answer questions on driving record, lifting and licensing progress, and the owner calls the fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they're hiring. Needs must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed account win-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Accounts that skipped last year's extinguisher inspection get a polite note and a route day, before their insurer asks."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs two years of account history.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the digital inspection report for extinguisher routes

routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want their service dealers busy and loyal.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: State fire equipment dealers association kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give members an inspection request page and reminder signup as a benefit. Fire safety dealers renew for tools they use daily."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One deal reaches many dealers in the state.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with a fire protection client start from a generic template. Mine has the inspection request, deficiency upload and tag reminders built in."

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "An inspection app someone started and dropped can usually be finished. I've already built the extinguisher report and tag-date logic."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Budget already approved; they need someone who knows fire safety paperwork.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your extinguisher technician course needs employers. A page listing local fire safety companies hiring graduates helps enrolment and placement."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training providers sell on placement, and the client is a hiring employer.
